previous_decisions.quote: In Zhang and Sternberg’s study, the mainland research participants rated intellectual styles as the most important resource for crea- tivity in their explicit evaluation of the six resources, while they indicated that intel- lectual styles would be the second most important resource when they evaluated the hypothetical cases. However, in the present study, whereas the Hong Kong partici- pants’ratings of boys were consistent with those in Zhang and Sternberg’s study, their ratings of girls were not.
previous_decisions.reason: The study set out to test whether two major types of findings from Zhang and Sternberg (2011a) replicated: (a) theory-practice discrepancies centred on intelligence and on intellectual styles, and (b) the gender gap in expectations. While the authors confirm the gender gap and find a smaller theory-practice gap on intelligence (stating later that the study 'largely replicated' the original findings), they explicitly contrast the girls' intellectual-style ratings in the hypothetical cases with Zhang and Sternberg (2011a), where intellectual style was the second most important resource across hypothetical cases but dropped to fourth/sixth for girls here. Under the codebook rules, when a tested finding is explicitly contrasted as differing from the original alongside other replicated findings, the outcome is 'mixed'.
